title: Elodie and the Static
premise: Silas Ishikawa, a xenolinguist whose dreams have begun arriving in an untranslatable alien tongue, tends a beacon on the fringe of a dying system-wide war between human colonies and the enigmatic Vessel-born. When gravity flickers for nine seconds across the entire system, the beacon activates a message it was built generations ago to deliver — and Silas discovers the beacon's true commissioner was their own grandmother, a Vessel-born hybrid erased from every record. To deliver the message before the reactor's countdown ends, Silas must decode the language they've been dreaming, cross a war zone, and confront the truth that the message is an inheritance: proof that both sides descend from the same lost ship. In the end, Silas broadcasts the message at the cost of the beacon and their own stored memories of it — ending the war, but leaving them unable to remember why it mattered, only that it did.
about_author: Wendell Lockridge is the pen name of a former radio telescope operator who spent a decade listening to static in the Atacama before turning to fiction. They write about people who maintain things nobody remembers building.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Weightlessness
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the beacon station Perihelion Rest, Silas logs routine maintenance while dreaming in a language they cannot name. Gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds; tools float, tea hangs in beads, and the beacon's ancient core wakes with a chime Silas has never heard. Beat: unease disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Commissioned
chapters.summary: Silas investigates the beacon's activation, finding maintenance logs in their grandmother's handwriting — a woman official records insist never existed. Their supervisor, Deputy Okafor, demands a report Silas can't honestly file. Beat: the first crack in the world Silas trusted.

chapters.title: Dreams with Grammar
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, intimate and fragmented. The dream-language returns nightly, and Silas, professionally unable to resist, begins transcribing it — discovering it has consistent phonology and, worse, consistent arguments. Beat: wonder shading into dread as the language starts addressing them directly.

chapters.title: War in the Long Dark
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Reza Voss, a colonial fleet officer escorting refugee barges through the Meridian Gap. Her brother died at Vessel hands; her orders are to shoot anything broadcasting on the old common band. Beat: the enemy made human before we ever meet them.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Back to Silas: the beacon's reactor, long dormant, spools up a countdown — 400 hours — tied to a transmission queue it cannot send while colonial jammers blanket the band. Okafor orders Silas to shut it down. Silas stalls. Beat: quiet insubordination.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hands
chapters.summary: Silas searches the station's physical archive — paper, deliberately analog — and finds their grandmother's research: she was Vessel-born, a hybrid, and the beacon is her life's work, a message addressed to both sides. Beat: grief and inheritance entangled.

chapters.title: The Language of the Vessel-Born
chapters.summary: Silas realizes the dream-language is not alien but ancestral — the lost mother-tongue of the ship both peoples descended from. The dreams are memories leaking through a genetic archive their grandmother seeded in the family line. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Convoy Meridian
chapters.summary: Reza's POV. Her convoy is ambushed by Vessel-born raiders who, strangely, take nothing — they broadcast a repeating phrase in an old language and leave. Reza records it, unable to translate it, and it haunts her. Beat: the enemy's message arrives at the reader before the hero.

chapters.title: Jamming
chapters.summary: Colonial command, spooked by the gravity flicker, doubles the jammers. Silas's transmission window shrinks; the countdown does not. Okafor, sympathetic but obedient, warns Silas that the next inspection will be lethal. Beat: walls closing in.

chapters.title: What Silas Forgot
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Silas discovers gaps in their own memory — childhood scenes that end mid-sentence, a sibling whose name they can't retrieve. Their grandmother's archive suggests the message requires a mind prepared to carry it, and preparation costs memory. Beat: the price is named.

chapters.title: Reza Hears the Static
chapters.summary: Reza plays the raiders' phrase against her brother's old letters and finds overlapping cadences — the Vessel-born tongue and colonial lullabies share roots. She files a translation request; command classifies it and orders her to forget it. Beat: a second doubter born.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Silas steals a maintenance skiff and descends toward the colonial relay hub to physically access the transmission array. The journey through debris fields from the war's first battle is harrowing and beautiful. Beat: commitment — no way back.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Reza's patrol intercepts the skiff. Interrogation becomes conversation when Silas answers her in the old language, and Reza recognizes it from the raiders' broadcast. She lets the skiff go and falsifies her log — her first act of mutiny. Beat: alliance forged in shared heresy.

chapters.title: The Relay Hub
chapters.summary: Silas reaches the hub and finds it half-abandoned, staffed by a skeleton crew of archivists who remember the beacon — and Silas's grandmother — from before the erasure. They offer help and a warning: command has flagged Silas as a Vessel asset. Beat: sanctuary with a timer on it.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Deputy Okafor, ordered to lead the arrest detail, arrives at the hub early — and chooses to warn Silas instead, giving them her command codes. She stays behind to face the consequences. Beat: sacrifice by the by-the-book character, earned.

chapters.title: Countdown: Six Hours
chapters.summary: Silas, in the array's core, decodes the final layer of the message: it is not a plea but a genealogy — proof both peoples descend from one lost ship, sealed with the grandmother's own hybrid genome. The reactor will burn out the beacon forever on transmission. Beat: the cost made concrete.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Colonial warships, Reza's among them, converge on the hub under orders to destroy it. Reza stalls her squadron with a false mechanical fault while Silas works. Vessel-born ships arrive on the opposite vector — drawn by the same signal. Beat: everything converges.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Silas transmits the genealogy on the old common band as both fleets power weapons. The message floods every dream-capable mind on both sides with shared ancestral memory — including Silas's, which burns away as it sends. Weapons hold. Beat: the message delivered at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Silence After
chapters.summary: The fleets stand down in stunned mutual recognition; commanders on both sides share the same inherited memory of the same lost crew. Reza docks at the hub and finds Silas alive but hollowed — unable to remember the beacon, the message, or why any of it mattered. Beat: victory and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Body Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas, memory-stripped, begins rebuilding from artifacts: their grandmother's papers, Okafor's testimony, Reza's recordings. They cannot recall the language — but when they sleep, they dream in it still, wordless now, and wake feeling they belong to something. Beat: grief metabolized into inheritance.

chapters.title: The New Commission
chapters.summary: Weeks later: armistice talks convene at the beacon, now a shared monument. Silas is asked to maintain it again — commissioned this time by both peoples, openly, with their name in the log beside their grandmother's restored record. Beat: belonging earned and recorded.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Silas's POV, quiet. Silas learns their erased sibling's name — Elodie — from the last page of the grandmother's archive, and speaks it aloud into the beacon's microphone, adding one word of their own to the inherited message. The static answers, gently. Beat: resolution — memory as an act of love, not a possession.
